evidence_note: S7 generates NO formal numbered evidence. It is the dress rehearsal for the S8 live Final Mission performance.

header.ambiente: Aula — centro despejado para ensayos por equipos + Word Wall visible + Role Cards visibles
header.nota: S7 = dress rehearsal. S8 = live Final Mission. Teams formed in S6-WHILE-D. Each team has assigned roles and bay.

final_mission_task_specification.title: The Diesel Workshop — Morning Readiness Briefing
final_mission_task_specification.subtitle: PM-3.5 Draft — Final Mission Task Card
final_mission_task_specification.scenario: Monday, 7:00 AM. Bay assigned by instructor. The Workshop Training Coordinator arrives for the morning inspection. Your team of 3 delivers the complete Bay Readiness Briefing in English.

responsibilities: Gives at least 2 instructions to the team (F1 — Imperatives)
Receives the final readiness report (F4) from team
Confirms team readiness and closes the briefing
Describes bay conditions (F3 — There is/are + prepositions)
Requests tools or help from Santiago (F2)
Responds to tool/help requests from Valentina (F2 response)

task_requirements: Duration: 3–4 minutes (minimum 3 min, maximum 4 min — strictly timed in S8)
All 5 language functions visible — minimum instances per role as specified above
≥ 15 Toolbelt terms used across the team (each distinct term counts once)
Team interaction: minimum 3 direct exchanges between team members (not 3 separate monologues)
There is/are + preposition in minimum 3 sentences
Bay-specific details: bay number, realistic conditions, plausible scenario
Closing: 'Bay ___ is ready. Briefing complete.' or equivalent

scoring_preview_s8.instrument: Escala de estimación No 6 — Observación directa (S8)
criteria_preview: All 5 language functions visible and used correctly
Team interaction — genuine exchanges, not monologues
Grammar accuracy: There is/are + prepositions + imperatives
Task completion: 3-4 min, bay identified, briefing closed
scoring_preview_s8.note: Full Escala No 6 finalized in S8 session plan.

final_mission_task_specification.sample_opening: CARLOS: 'Good morning. Bay 2 Readiness Briefing. Valentina — check the floor jack. Santiago — PPE check. Let's go.' (F1 × 2)
final_mission_task_specification.sample_interaction: VALENTINA: 'Santiago, can I have the torque wrench?' / SANTIAGO: 'Here you go. The goggles are on the workbench, Valentina.' / VALENTINA: 'There is a spill near the bay door. I'll clean it now.' (F2, F3, F5)
final_mission_task_specification.sample_closing: VALENTINA: 'Bay 2 is ready, Carlos. Checklist: complete.' / CARLOS: 'Excellent. Bay 2 — briefing complete. Team dismissed.' (F4, F4-response)

peer_observation_sheet.title: Peer Observation Sheet — Final Mission Rehearsal
peer_observation_sheet.instructions: Observer: watch your team's rehearsal. Fill in the sheet DURING the performance. Give feedback immediately after.

sections.tally: Count each distinct term you hear: ___ / 15 minimum

sections.direct_exchanges: How many times did team members speak DIRECTLY to each other? ___ / 3 minimum
sections.note: Monologue = one person talking without pause. Exchange = two people talking back and forth.

sections.strength: One thing the team did WELL: ___
sections.note: Be specific. 'Good job' is NOT helpful feedback. 'You used F3 twice — add one more There is/are' IS helpful.

role_card_template.title: Role Card — Final Mission
fields: My 3 key sentences (write your OWN — not from the model):
My 5 Toolbelt terms I will use: ___, ___, ___, ___, ___
My cue from Carlos: (what does Carlos say that triggers my first line?): ___
My transition to Santiago/Valentina: (what do I say to pass the floor?): ___
role_card_template.instructor_note: Role Cards are NOT a script. They are a preparation tool. Students should be able to speak naturally by S8 — the card is training wheels, not the performance itself.

focused_mini_drills.description: Targeted drills for WHILE-C — address specific weaknesses identified in Round 1 feedback

drill_menu.focus: F3 expansion — not enough There is/are
drill_menu.drill: Bay image flash: instructor shows bay image (5 sec) → teams race to say 3 There is/are sentences. Fastest team with 3 correct = point.
Turn-taking chain: Carlos says F1 → Valentina responds F5 + adds F3 → Santiago responds F2 → Carlos closes F4. No one speaks twice in a row. 2 rounds.

drill_menu.focus: Toolbelt term density — too few terms
drill_menu.drill: Toolbelt sprint: pairs have 90 seconds to build a 4-sentence report using as many Toolbelt terms as possible. Count and report to group.
Expansion challenge: take a 90-second report from S4 and add 3 new exchanges between team members to reach 3 minutes. Role-play the expanded version.
Chunk Cards rapid review: fire extinguisher / preventive maintenance / calibration / torque wrench / floor jack. Orchestral drill × 2 rounds.

focused_mini_drills.instructor_note: Select 2-3 drills from this menu based on Round 1 peer feedback data. Do NOT do all 5 — choose the highest-impact drills for the specific teams in the room.

set_up.title: Final Mission Launch — Teams, Roles, Mission Brief

teacher_talk.opening: Good morning, Workshop Team. This is Session 7 — Final Mission Preparation. Tomorrow, you perform. Today, you prepare. By the end of today, you will be ready.
teacher_talk.context: You formed your teams in S6. You know your roles — Carlos, Valentina, Santiago. Today you will rehearse THREE times, get feedback each time, and finish with a Role Card that is YOURS — written in your voice, ready for S8.
teacher_talk.stakes_setting: In S8, I am no longer your instructor. I am the Training Coordinator — an outside evaluator. You are the team. The bay is real. The briefing is real. Today — practice. Tomorrow — perform.
teacher_talk.icq: ICQ — How many rehearsals today? (three) Who gives feedback? (your peers, then me) Can you use notes during S8? (no — Word Wall yes, notes no) How long is the Final Mission? (3 to 4 minutes)

activities.procedure: Teams from S6 regroup — verify membership (3 per team, Carlos/Valentina/Santiago roles). If any changes needed (absent student in S6 → reassign role) — resolve now. Instructor assigns bay number to each team (Bay 1, 2, or 3) — different from their S4 individual bay where possible. Each team writes: TEAM NAME (optional) + BAY + ROLES on whiteboard corner or paper.
activities.facilitation_note: 💡 Bay assignment should be done quickly and definitively — do not let teams negotiate or swap at length. A team that argues about bay assignment is avoiding preparation. 'Bay 2 — done. Next.'

activities.activity: Final Mission Task Card — Read + Clarify
activities.procedure: Distribute Final Mission Task Card (or project). Teams read individually (2 min) — then 3 clarifying questions to instructor maximum. Instructor reads requirements aloud, pausing at each: 'Three to four minutes — timed. Fifteen Toolbelt terms minimum — across all three of you. Three direct exchanges — meaning YOU talk to EACH OTHER, not only to me.' Answer questions briefly — do not over-explain.
activities.facilitation_note: 💡 Students may ask: 'Can we use the Word Wall?' — Yes, in S8 as well (same as Evidence 5). 'Do we need a script?' — No. A Role Card with key phrases yes, a full script no. 'What if someone forgets?' — Keep going, help each other. That is ALSO workshop communication.

activities.procedure: Write on board: Round 1 (WHILE-B) → Peer Feedback → Mini-Drills (WHILE-C) → Round 2 → Break → Round 3: Instructor Feedback (WHILE-D) → Role Card Finalization (WHILE-E). Assign peer observers: for each team's Round 1, one member from the NEXT team in the rotation observes with the Peer Observation Sheet. Explain peer observer role: 'You are helping your colleagues prepare. Your feedback counts — be honest and specific.'
activities.formative_checkpoint: ✓ All teams formed and bay-assigned. ✓ Task Card distributed and requirements understood. ✓ Peer observer rotation established.

while_a.title: Team Strategy + Role Card Draft
while_a.purpose: Cada equipo analiza la tarea, asigna funciones específicas a cada rol, redacta borrador del Role Card y practica apertura y cierre de la sesión

teacher_talk.instruction: Teams — 55 minutes. Your job: build your plan. Who says what. When. In what order. Write your Role Card draft. Then practice JUST the opening and closing — not the full performance yet.
teacher_talk.transition: By 08:10 — every team should have done the opening at least twice. I will check before we move to Round 1.
teacher_talk.icq: ICQ — What is on the Role Card? (my 3 key sentences, my 5 Toolbelt terms, my cue, my transition) Should you write a full script? (no — key phrases only)

activities.activity: Role Card Draft — Individual then Team
activities.procedure: Each student completes their own Role Card draft (15 min individual): (1) circle role name, (2) write bay number, (3) draft 3 key sentences using their assigned language functions, (4) list 5 Toolbelt terms they will use, (5) write their cue (what Carlos says that triggers them) and transition (how they pass the floor). Then teams compare Role Cards (10 min): check for function coverage — does the team collectively cover all 5 functions? Does the team collectively use 15+ distinct Toolbelt terms? Adjust any gaps.
activities.facilitation_note: 💡 Walk team by team during draft time. The most common gap: Santiago's role card is too thin — students playing Santiago often write 2 sentences and feel 'done.' Push Santiago: 'You are a TECHNICIAN — you know the tools, the conditions, the problems. What does Santiago see that the others don't?' Santiago should have 3 substantive contributions, not just F5 filler responses.
activities.formative_checkpoint: ✓ Every student has a written Role Card draft before team comparison begins.

activities.procedure: Teams practice ONLY the opening (first 30 seconds) and closing (last 20 seconds) of their briefing — not the full middle section. Round 1: read from Role Card. Round 2: without looking at Role Card. Target: opening is natural and confident before Round 1 begins. Instructor circulates — listens to 2-3 openings, gives 1 micro-correction per team if needed (one small fix, not a rewrite).
activities.opening_frame: Carlos: greeting + bay ID + 2 instructions. Valentina: first confirm. Santiago: first confirm or F3 observation. Goal: first 5 exchanges feel automatic.
activities.closing_frame: Valentina: final F4 report to Carlos. Carlos: acknowledge + close. Goal: clean, confident ending — not trailing off.
activities.facilitation_note: 💡 Teams that nail the opening and closing carry the confidence into the middle. A shaky opening = anxiety throughout. A clean closing = positive memory. Prioritize these two anchors above all else in WHILE-A.

activities.procedure: Teams audit their Role Cards: list all distinct Toolbelt terms across all three cards. Count. If under 15: identify the gap categories (which of the 5 Toolbelt categories is under-represented?) and assign 2-3 additional terms to specific roles. If over 15: good — don't reduce, celebrate the abundance.
activities.facilitation_note: 💡 Teams often over-load on TOOLS and under-use MAINTENANCE and DOCUMENTS. Remind them: 'preventive maintenance checklist: complete' is one phrase that covers 3 Toolbelt terms — efficient and professional.

differentiation.fast_finishers: After opening+closing practice — do a complete first run-through (full 3-4 min) internally, unobserved. Self-time it. Identify the slowest/most hesitant moment and drill it separately.
differentiation.more_support: Teams with a missing member (absent) or a very struggling student: instructor assigns a simplified Role Card — fewer required functions (F3 + F4 + F5 minimum instead of full set) — full functions targeted by S8.

while_a.tecnica_didactica: Taller de práctica / Lectura de especificación de tarea

while_b.title: Round 1 Rehearsal — Full Run + Peer Feedback
while_b.purpose: Primera rehearsal cronometrada completa de cada equipo — observación de pares con Peer Observation Sheet — retroalimentación específica inmediata

teacher_talk.instruction: Round 1. Each team performs their full Final Mission Briefing — 3 to 4 minutes. I am watching. Your peer observer is watching. After each team: 3 minutes of peer feedback — specific, actionable. Then: next team.
teacher_talk.during_performance: (silence — instructor marks notes, peer observer marks sheet)
teacher_talk.after_each_performance: Peer observer — share your sheet. What functions did you see? How many Toolbelt terms? Duration? One strength. One suggestion. Team — listen. Do NOT argue. Write down the suggestion.
teacher_talk.icq: ICQ — Can you stop and restart during Round 1? (no — finish the full briefing even if you make an error) What does the team do during peer feedback? (listen and write)

logistics.performance_order: Teams draw numbers in SET-UP or instructor assigns. Rotation: while Team A performs, Team B peer-observes, Team C prepares quietly.
logistics.time_per_team: 4 min performance + 3 min feedback + 2 min transition = ~9 min per team
logistics.timer_protocol: Start timer when Carlos says first word. Call time at 4:00 min if team has not closed. Note if team finished under 3 min — that is a critical data point for WHILE-C.

what_to_watch: Which function is visibly missing or weak across most teams?
Which teams have monologue problem (one person doing 80% of the talking)?
Which teams are under 3 min? Which are over 4 min?
Which 3-4 Toolbelt terms are NOT appearing across teams?
instructor_observation_focus.what_to_note: Brief notes per team — these drive the Mini-Drill selection in WHILE-C. Do NOT give verbal feedback during Round 1 — only after all teams have performed.

post_round_whole_class.procedure: Quick class-wide data share: (1) Duration check: 'How many teams finished under 3 minutes? Raise hand.' (2) 'How many teams had all 5 functions observed by the peer?' (3) 'Most common missing function? Call it out.' Instructor synthesizes: 'In WHILE-C — after break — we drill [2 specific targets]. Then Round 2.'
post_round_whole_class.facilitation_note: 💡 This whole-class debrief is the critical pivot between Round 1 and Round 2. It transforms individual team feedback into class-wide insight. Students realize their 'weakness' is often shared — this normalizes struggle and focuses collective effort.

differentiation.fast_finishers: Team finished strong with all 5 functions + 15 terms: peer observer writes 3 specific linguistic improvements (word choice, preposition accuracy, grammar) rather than function-level feedback.
differentiation.more_support: If a team freezes during Round 1: instructor says one word ('Continue.') to restart. Does NOT provide the missing line. Post-performance: instructor sits with the team for 2 min of targeted coaching — identify the specific moment of freeze and rehearse that transition.

while_b.tecnica_didactica: Ensayo guiado en equipo de 3 + Peer Observation Sheet

break.instructor_note: During break: (1) Review notes from Round 1 observations. (2) Select 2-3 targeted drills from the drill_menu in session_assets based on class-wide gaps. (3) Arrange drill materials. Students should NOT rehearse during break — cognitive rest is productive before Round 2.
break.transition_back: Welcome back. Before Round 2 — two focused drills based on what we saw. Short, fast, specific. Then Round 2.

while_c.title: Targeted Drills + Round 2 Rehearsal
while_c.purpose: Drills focalizados en las 2-3 debilidades identificadas en Round 1 — luego segunda rehearsal completa incorporando feedback y drills

teacher_talk.instruction: Two drills — fast. You will feel the improvement immediately. Then Round 2: same structure, same time limit. Your peer observer will be a DIFFERENT student this time — fresh eyes.
teacher_talk.transition_to_round2: Drills done. Round 2. New observer. Full performance. Go.
teacher_talk.icq: ICQ — Should Round 2 be different from Round 1? (yes — incorporate the feedback) Can you use your Role Card during Round 2? (yes — but try to minimize)

activities.procedure: Instructor selects 2-3 drills from session_assets.focused_mini_drills based on Round 1 class-wide gaps. Run each drill whole-class (not per team). Fast, energetic, competitive where appropriate. Each drill: model once, then run. Do not debrief drills — keep momentum.
activities.default_selection: If instructor did not take notes during Round 1: default to (1) F3 expansion drill (10 min) + (2) Team interaction chain drill (12 min) — these are the two highest-frequency gaps in A1.1 speaking simulations.
activities.facilitation_note: 💡 Drills work best when they are FASTER than the actual performance pace. Pressure in drill = fluency in performance. If a drill feels too slow or comfortable, make it faster or add a consequence (losing a Toolbelt term from your allowed list if you hesitate).

activities.procedure: Same rotation structure as Round 1 — 9 min per team (4 min performance + 3 min feedback + 2 min transition). Peer observer is a DIFFERENT student from Round 1 (rotated within team or from adjacent team). Peer uses same Peer Observation Sheet. Focus for Round 2 feedback: did the team address the Round 1 weakness? Name it specifically: 'In Round 1 you had 2 F3 sentences. In Round 2 I heard ___.'
activities.instructor_focus_round2: Watch for: (1) Teams that got WORSE in Round 2 — usually means they overthought the feedback (reassure: 'Natural is better than perfect'). (2) Teams that are right at 3 min now — they have room to expand in S8. (3) Any student still reading the Role Card heavily — they need focused prep in WHILE-E.
activities.formative_checkpoint: ✓ All teams completed Round 2. ✓ All Peer Observation Sheets for Round 2 collected or held by teams. ✓ Instructor has notes on per-team progress between Round 1 and Round 2.

differentiation.fast_finishers: After Round 2 — team identifies one moment in the performance where they could use a HIGHER Bloom level (L4 Analyze) — e.g., instead of describing a condition, also explaining WHY it is a risk. Draft and practice that one extension.
differentiation.more_support: Before Round 2: instructor sits with struggling team for 3 min during tail end of drills. Identifies one manageable fix (not a full rewrite): e.g., 'Just add THIS ONE SENTENCE before your F4 report: There are two tools on the workbench. Try it now.'

while_c.tecnica_didactica: Simulación con retroalimentación estructurada entre pares (3 categorías)

while_d.title: Round 3 — Dress Rehearsal with Instructor Feedback
while_d.purpose: Tercera y última rehearsal — instructor actúa como Training Coordinator (evaluador externo) — feedback individual escrito por equipo — simulación más cercana a condiciones de S8

teacher_talk.mode_shift: From this point — I am the Training Coordinator. I am not your instructor. I do not help you. I observe. I evaluate. I write. After your briefing — I will give you a written feedback card. This is the dress rehearsal. Treat it as real.
teacher_talk.during_performance: (Instructor observes in silence. Takes written notes. No reactions during performance.)
teacher_talk.post_performance: (After each team finishes) 'Thank you, team.' (writes 60 seconds) 'Three things: one strength — [specific]. One improvement — [specific + actionable]. One question for you: [a follow-up question about their bay/report]. Prepare to answer that question in S8.'
teacher_talk.icq: ICQ — Can you ask me for help during Round 3? (no — I am the Training Coordinator, not your instructor) What do you do if you forget a line? (keep going, your team helps you)

activities.activity: Round 3 — Dress Rehearsal (Instructor as Training Coordinator)
activities.procedure: Instructor takes seat as outside observer — NOT at the front of the room. Teams perform as in Rounds 1-2 but with upgraded conditions: (1) No peer observer peer form — this is instructor-evaluated. (2) Word Wall visible but no other materials for reference. (3) Instructor uses Round 3 Feedback Card per team (see below) — fills it in real-time. (4) After each team: 2-min verbal feedback maximum (key points only — full written card given at end). Rotation: ~10 min per team.

fields: Functions observed: F1✓✗ F2✓✗ F3✓✗ F4✓✗ F5✓✗
Follow-up question for S8: (a question the team must be ready to answer in S8): ___

follow_up_question_bank: Where is the ratchet right now?
What type of maintenance does this vehicle need?
Is there any hazard I should know about?
How many tools are in the toolbox?
activities.facilitation_note: 💡 The follow-up question is the secret weapon of Round 3. It reveals whether students have truly internalized the scenario or are just reciting. The question should be simple enough to answer with Toolbelt vocabulary — but students who are only reciting a script will freeze. In S8, you will ask the same question (or a variant). Tell teams after Round 3: 'I will ask you a question like this in S8. Prepare your answer.'
activities.formative_checkpoint: ✓ All teams completed Round 3. ✓ Instructor feedback card written for each team.

activities.activity: Distribute Round 3 Feedback Cards + Brief Whole-Class Debrief
activities.procedure: Distribute written feedback cards to teams. 5 min: teams read and discuss their card. Then whole-class (5 min): 'One class-wide strength I observed across all teams.' + 'One class-wide improvement before S8.' + 'You are ready. S8 is the performance.'
activities.facilitation_note: 💡 The class-wide strength is not a consolation prize — it should be genuinely observed and specific. 'Every team used There is/are at least twice' is more powerful than 'Great job everyone.' Students need to know specifically what they are doing right.

differentiation.fast_finishers: Team received all ✓ on Round 3 feedback card: prepare 2 extended responses for the follow-up question bank — practice answering with 2-3 sentences rather than 1.
differentiation.more_support: Team with critical gaps after Round 3: instructor schedules 10-min one-on-one team coaching in first 10 min of S8 before performance rotation begins. Note on feedback card: 'See me first in S8.'

while_d.tecnica_didactica: Práctica de campo (segundo ensayo con incorporación de feedback)

while_e.title: Role Card Finalization + Pronunciation Polish + S8 Briefing
while_e.purpose: Finalizar Role Cards definitivos basados en 3 rounds de feedback; polish final de pronunciación; briefing logístico de S8; asignación de trabajo autónomo

teacher_talk.instruction: Final 55 minutes. Three things: finalize your Role Card — this is the version you take home tonight and use in S8. Pronunciation — 5 target terms, last drill of the session. Then: everything you need to know about S8.
teacher_talk.motivation: You have rehearsed three times. You have received peer feedback, instructor feedback, a follow-up question. You know exactly what to do. Tonight — rest, review your card, say your lines aloud once. Tomorrow — perform.

activities.procedure: Students revise Role Card based on Round 3 feedback card. Final version must: (a) be in their own words (no copying model script), (b) include their assigned functions with real examples, (c) include their specific follow-up question answer (2-3 sentences). Students write FINAL on top of card. Cards are NOT collected — they belong to the student. They carry the card home and to S8 (for reference before performance, not during).
activities.facilitation_note: 💡 Students who want to memorize a script will copy the model from the task card or the board. Redirect: 'Cross out anything I wrote. Write it in YOUR voice. If Carlos usually says 'Check it' instead of 'Check the floor jack now' — write YOURS.' Authenticity > perfection at A1.1.

activities.procedure: Chunk Cards rapid review: fire extinguisher / preventive maintenance / calibration / torque wrench / floor jack. Orchestral drill — 2 rounds each (full sequence: model → class → left/right → pairs → solo volunteers). Then: each team says all 5 terms in a chain — one term per person, relay style. Last: instructor points to a random Word Wall term — first student to say it correctly with correct pronunciation earns 1 point for their team.

pronunciation_notes.fire_extinguisher: Most common error: 'exTINGUIHer' — ensure final /ʃər/ not /ʃer/
pronunciation_notes.preventive_maintenance: Most common error: stress on wrong syllable — pre-VEN-tive, not PRE-ventive
pronunciation_notes.calibration: Usually clean by S7 — use as confidence builder
pronunciation_notes.torque_wrench: Most common error: pronouncing the 'u' in 'torque' — TORK only
pronunciation_notes.floor_jack: Most common error: Spanish 'j' sound — English /dʒ/ as in 'judge'

activities.activity: S8 Full Briefing — Logistics, Conditions, Schedule
activities.procedure: Instructor presents S8 logistics: (1) Performance order: teams draw numbers or assigned by instructor. (2) Waiting area: teams waiting perform a final silent Role Card review — no speaking rehearsal (to avoid voice fatigue and to maintain performance conditions). (3) Observer condition: remaining students observe using a simplified observation sheet — not graded, for their learning. (4) Follow-up question: I will ask one question from the question bank per team. (5) After all teams perform: Full Circle activities — Gap Cards, reflection, celebration. (6) Word Wall is visible. Communication Card from S5 is NOT permitted — it is a language support, not a performance aid.

s8_schedule_preview.SET-UP: Return Round 3 feedback cards + S8 conditions review + team last prep (15 min)
s8_schedule_preview.Performances: Teams in order — 4 min per team + follow-up question + transition (~8 min/team)
s8_schedule_preview.Full_Circle: Gap Cards redistribution + KWL completion + Skills reflection + celebration

activities.facilitation_note: 💡 The waiting condition is pedagogically critical: teams that watch other teams perform learn from them in real time. If Team C watches Team B nail F3, they will add it to their own performance. Allow and encourage this — it is the most natural form of peer learning.

differentiation.fast_finishers: Compose a written version of their S8 follow-up question answer — this doubles as study material for tonight and ensures a clean verbal answer in S8.
differentiation.more_support: Student who is significantly weaker than the team: instructor privately adjusts role scope — e.g., Santiago's role is simplified to 3 core lines (F2 + F5 + one F3) that are fully rehearsed rather than attempting everything and freezing. Full role attempted in S8 autonomo if time permits.

while_e.tecnica_didactica: Drills de pronunciación con Chunk Cards + consolidación iterativa de role cards

teacher_talk.closing: Three rehearsals. Three rounds of feedback. A Role Card you wrote yourself. Pronunciation that is clear and professional. Tonight — review the card. Say your lines once out loud. Sleep. Tomorrow — perform.
teacher_talk.final_words: In S8, I am not your instructor. I am the Training Coordinator. But I know — because I watched you today — that you are ready. Bay ___, Bay ___, Bay ___ — all ready.
teacher_talk.motivation: You started this guide saying three words you knew in English about a workshop. Tomorrow you will give a 3-to-4-minute professional briefing in English. That is the proof of what learning looks like.

activities.procedure: Each team writes on the board their team motto or team name in English (any phrase that represents their team spirit). Then: each team member writes one word on a sticky note: 'I feel ___ about S8.' Post sticky notes on 'S8 Ready Wall'. Instructor reads 3 aloud (anonymous) — respond to any fears openly: 'Nervous is normal. It means you care. That is a good sign.'
activities.facilitation_note: 💡 The 'nervous' sticky notes are almost certain to appear. Do not dismiss them ('Don't worry, you'll be fine!'). Acknowledge: 'Nervous means the performance matters. Channel it into energy. Carlos — take a breath before you start. Valentina — look at your team, not at me. Santiago — you know this.'

activities.procedure: Distribute or write autonomous work assignment. Also give each student a 'S8 Final Checklist': Role Card ✓ / Follow-up question answer ✓ / 5 pronunciation terms practiced ✓ / Full briefing said aloud once tonight ✓ / Team contact confirmed (any last-minute changes) ✓.
activities.facilitation_note: 💡 The S8 checklist is both a practical tool and a psychological anchor. Students who complete it before arriving feel prepared. Students who don't — will feel it.

activities.procedure: Final logistics: start time, room, order will be confirmed at start of S8. Remind: 'Word Wall visible in S8. No notes during performance. Timing starts when Carlos opens. Finish clean.' Dismiss with: 'See you in The Diesel Workshop. Final session. Full circle.'
activities.formative_checkpoint: ✓ All teams have finalized Role Cards. ✓ Round 3 Feedback Cards distributed. ✓ S8 logistics communicated. ✓ Autonomous work assigned.

materials_checklist: Final Mission Task Card — 1 per student (or projected)
Peer Observation Sheet — 2 per student (Round 1 + Round 2)
Round 3 Feedback Card — 1 per team (instructor completes)
Sticky notes — 1 per student (S8 Ready Wall)
Whiteboard space for team names + role assignments
logistics_box.room_setup: Center space clear for performances. Teams seated in clusters. Observer area (non-performing team) has clear sightlines to performance space. Word Wall visible from performance area.
logistics_box.technology: Projector for Final Mission Task Card + drill images (F3 bay images if using that drill). Timer projected or instructor-held.

plan_b.if_a_team_is_missing_a_member: Redistribute roles: Carlos + Valentina perform (2-person version with abbreviated Santiago lines distributed between them). This is still evaluable in S8 — instructor notes in Escala No 6.
plan_b.if_WHILE_B_takes_longer: Reduce post-round whole-class debrief to 2 min (just the duration and missing functions vote). Save up to 8 min.
plan_b.if_WHILE_C_drills_not_needed: If all teams performed strongly in Round 1 (all 5 functions observed, 15+ terms, 3+ exchanges): skip drills, begin Round 2 immediately. Use saved time for a second Round 3 (instructor feedback) — give best teams a final stretch challenge.
plan_b.if_WHILE_D_runs_long: If teams are taking longer than 4 min each: after 4:30 min, instructor says 'Close the briefing' to the performing team. Do not allow indefinite extension — timing is part of the task.
plan_b.if_students_are_highly_anxious_about_s8: Use last 5 min of WRAP-UP for a 'confidence circle': each team says one thing they will do WELL in S8. Instructor affirms specifically. End on a forward-looking, positive note.

actividades: Revisar el Role Card finalizado — leerlo en voz alta una vez como si fuera S8. Cronometrar la parte individual del reporte (debe ser ~60-80 seg de los 3-4 min totales del equipo).
Preparar la respuesta a la follow-up question del Feedback Card Round 3 — escribirla y practicarla en voz alta (2-3 oraciones, sin leer).
Practicar los 5 términos de pronunciación: fire extinguisher / preventive maintenance / calibration / torque wrench / floor jack — una vez en oraciones completas.

Revisar tu Communication Card: marca cuál de las 5 funciones lingüísticas dominas MÁS y cuál dominas MENOS. Escribe una oración adicional de ejemplo para tu función más débil — úsala en el reporte del Final Mission S8.

Releer el artículo 'Tools Every Diesel Technician Needs.' Identifica 3 preguntas del Cuestionario S6 donde no estabas seguro/a de tu respuesta. Para cada una, encuentra la respuesta en el texto y copia la oración que la sustenta.

Con tu equipo (por mensaje o en persona), finaliza el borrador del Workshop Readiness Report: (1) qué bahía reportan, (2) quién dice qué, (3) dónde aparece cada una de las 5 funciones lingüísticas. Trae el outline listo para S8.

questions: ¿Completaron los 3 rounds de rehearsal todos los equipos, con Peer Observation Sheet en R1+R2 y Feedback Card en R3?
¿Seleccioné y ejecuté 2-3 mini-drills focalizados en las debilidades reales de Round 1 (no los drills por defecto)?
¿Cada equipo tiene una follow-up question específica en su Feedback Card para preparar antes de S8?
¿Todos los estudiantes tienen un Role Card finalizado en su propia voz (no una copia del modelo)?
¿Están claros los logísticos de S8 para todos: orden de performance, condiciones, Word Wall visible, timing?

after_s7.note: No new skills completed in S7 — all 7 skills already marked ● after S6. S7 deepens Speaking, Vocabulary, Grammar integration in preparation for S8 Final Mission.

feeds_from: S4 — Stock Cards (reusable reference for bay status in role cards)
S4 — Workshop Readiness Report format (individual → expanded to team in Final Mission)
S5 — Evidence 5 simulation structure (team roles + 5 functions → direct predecessor to Final Mission)
S6 — Team formation (teams formed in S6-WHILE-D)
S6 — Round 3 follow-up question bank (instructor designs S8 questions from same bank)
feeds_into: S8 — The Full Circle: Final Mission live performance + Gap Cards redistribution + closure
PM-3.5 Final: the Final Mission task card designed here becomes the definitive S8 instrument
connections.economía_principle: Role Cards created in S7 carried into S8. Gap Cards from S1 still plastified — redistributed in S8 (not S7). Word Wall permanent since S2 — visible and active in S7 + S8.

justificacion_didactica: Los ensayos en S7 son ensayos de transferencia controlada: el aprendiz aplica todo lo aprendido en S1-S6 en un entorno simulado del sector productivo con retroalimentación inmediata entre pares y del instructor.

grammar_groups: Grupos 1, 2, 5, 7: producción integrada en el borrador de la Final Mission.
Revisión de Grupo 1 (be) como estructura de anclaje para la presentación oral.

feedback.mode: COACHING — feedback formativo orientado a mejorar el borrador. Mezcla de accuracy y fluency.
accuracy_techniques: Feedback escrito en el borrador: usar error codes (G, V, WO, Sp) con comentario específico.
Peer feedback estructurado: aprendiz A corrige borrador de B con el mismo error code system.
Metalinguistic cue en conferencia individual: señalar el tipo de error, aprendiz busca la regla en PM-0.
fluency_techniques: Rehearsal oral de la Final Mission: modo fluency completo. Instructor observa sin interrumpir.
Self-assessment con rúbrica: aprendiz evalúa su propio borrador antes de la conferencia.
feedback.notes: S7 es preparación, no evaluación. El aprendiz DEBE cometer errores aquí — es el momento seguro para fallar y corregir antes de S8.

l1_management.l1_percentage: ≤ 10 % L1. Aprendices deben poder dar el ensayo de su presentación completamente en inglés.
l1_management.english_zone_declaration: English Zone estricta durante todos los rehearsals. 'Si olvidas una palabra — paraphrase. Di algo diferente en inglés. No cambies al español.'
l1_allowed_for: Conferencia individual de feedback escrito si hay error conceptual grave.
Auto-reflexión metacognitiva al final (puede ser en español).
l1_management.reduction_strategy: Técnica de paraphrase: cuando el aprendiz se bloquea en inglés, instructor pregunta '¿Cómo lo dirías diferente en inglés?' — no acepta la traducción directa.

techniques: Rehearsal con grabación de voz: aprendices se graban en celular y escuchan su propio stress.
Backchaining de la oración de apertura de la presentación.
Clapping del ritmo de la frase de conclusión: 'In CON-clu-sion, the WORK-shop IS now SAFE.'
Peer pronunciation coach: un aprendiz escucha y señala con pulgar arriba/abajo si el stress es correcto.
stress_pronunciation.board_marking: Frase de apertura con marcado de stress: 'I AM the WORK-shop SPE-cial-ist for BAY TWO.'
stress_pronunciation.notes: El nerviosismo en S8 hace que el aprendiz hable rápido y pierda el stress. S7 es el momento de anclar el ritmo.

factors_applied: S — Sounds: drill de las frases de transición con entonación de presentación.
U — Use: aprendices incorporan cada frase en su borrador durante S7.
C — Creativity: crear una apertura y cierre personalizados para su presentación.
S — Self-expression: el borrador ES la voz del aprendiz sobre su taller específico.
